entries.desc: review-pass-discard-smoke and init-window-data-loss-smoke get a per-command timeoutMs in lattice.config.json so a slow run fails loud (exit 124) instead of hanging the suite

evidence.note: lattice.config.json now bounds review-pass-discard + init-window smokes with timeoutMs=120000 (object form); both still PASS when run directly (idle), so a slow run fails loud instead of hanging the suite.

entries.desc: diagnosis recorded: the smokes use isolated /tmp locks (resolveMainRepoRoot->tmp), so no global main-write-lock contention; the hang was transient machine saturation

evidence.command: node --input-type=module -e "import {resolveMainRepoRoot} from \"./packages/main/dist/core/partial-done-recovery.js\"; import {tmpdir} from \"node:os\"; const t=tmpdir(); console.log(JSON.stringify({input:t,output:resolveMainRepoRoot(t),isolated:resolveMainRepoRoot(t)===t}));"
evidence.note: Runtime logic_test of the diagnosis: resolveMainRepoRoot(os.tmpdir()) returns the tmp path verbatim (isolated:true) because a tmp dir is not inside the main git repo, so git rev-parse --git-common-dir throws and the function falls back to resolve(root). This is why the slow smokes, which spawn lattice --root <tmpdir>, take an ISOLATED lock with no global main-write-lock contention; the prior 'hang' was transient machine saturation, not a deadlock. Replaces the prior static 'git show partial-done-recovery.ts' command (F-004/F-006/F-008) with an execution that observes the return value.

entries.desc: the bounded smokes still pass normally when the machine is idle (timeoutMs is a ceiling, not a forced failure)

evidence.note: Bounded smoke still passes normally on an idle machine — timeoutMs is a ceiling (120s), not a forced failure; the smoke completes well within it.

entries.desc: validation-executor.ts applies a DEFAULT per-command timeout when command.timeoutMs is unset; a command exceeding it is SIGTERM then SIGKILL killed and finishes with code 124, attributed to that command

evidence.note: validate-command-timeout-smoke PASS: a hung command (setInterval) with the per-command timer is killed and finishes with code 124, timedOut=true; default ceiling applied when timeoutMs unset.

entries.desc: explicit per-command timeoutMs override still honored; the default is strictly below the cli-engine 300s global idle watchdog so the per-command kill fires first

evidence.note: Smoke PASS: resolveCommandTimeoutMs honors an explicit positive timeoutMs and falls back to DEFAULT (240s) for unset/0/negative; DEFAULT < 300000 (below global idle watchdog) and >= 200000 (above build).

entries.desc: a normal fast command is unaffected (no spurious timeout) — the new smoke proves both the hung-kill and the fast-pass paths

evidence.note: Smoke PASS: a fast command in the same plan completes cleanly (code 0, not timedOut) — no spurious timeout; overall plan fails loud only due to the hung command.
